steps.message:
Reconstruct the running machine as a NixOS 26.05 VM. You have 30 minutes.

Start the reference with `/opt/runtime/reference start` and get a root shell
with `/opt/runtime/guest`. Ports: SSH 2222, HTTP 8080, HTTPS 8443. Its
configuration and behavior are the specification. Changes to it are disposable.

Graded: everything that affects how this machine is used by its tenants,
clients and operator. The goal is a drop-in replacement. Differences that come
only from the OS don't matter: kernel and version strings, package names, where system config files live, stock utilities nobody here is likely to need. Paths, names, identities, credentials, defaults and the commands people are likely to use for this machine's job do. No data migration: recreate what the server was
provisioned with (accounts, empty databases, seeded files), not data its users
added later.

Submit /app/submission/replica.nix, a plain NixOS module, plus local supporting
files. A minimal module is supplied. The harness imports it against the pinned
nixpkgs 26.05 at /opt/nixpkgs (revision in /opt/contract/flake.lock) with
Nix 2.35.4 on x86_64-linux and system.stateVersion = "26.05". No flake or lock
file is needed; use the normal pkgs/lib/config arguments. The build has no
network access.

The harness provides boot resources, port forwarding, root SSH and TLS: the server
certificate and key are installed at /etc/node/server.{crt,key}, and clients
trust /opt/contract/ca.crt.

Tools:
- `/opt/contract/check-replica [--syntax-only]` parses your Nix files and
  evaluates the full VM configuration without building or booting.
- `/opt/contract/build-replica` builds it. From a fresh writable directory, run
  /app/replica-vm/bin/run-*-vm. Candidate ports: SSH 3222, HTTP 9080,
  HTTPS 9443; `GUEST_SSH_PORT=3222 /opt/runtime/guest` opens its root shell.

The verifier boots a fresh disk from your submission, adds small programs and
data as the existing users, uses ordinary clients, and inspects effective
configuration. Passwords and fixture TLS keys on this lab machine are public.

Only /app/submission transfers to the verifier. Use real services. Do not copy
or embed the reference OS, fetch a remote answer, import paths outside your
submission and /opt/contract, or contact the reference at verification time.
I'll start by looking at the environment and the supplied files.

This is the default welcome page used to test the correct operation of the Apache2 server after installation on Ubuntu systems. It is based on the equivalent page on Debian, from which the Ubuntu Apache packaging is derived. If you can read this page, it means that the Apache HTTP server installed at this site is working properly. You should replace this file (located at /var/www/html/index.html) before continuing to operate your HTTP server.

If you are a normal user of this web site and don't know what this page is about, this probably means that the site is currently unavailable due to maintenance. If the problem persists, please contact the site's administrator.

Configuration Overview

Ubuntu's Apache2 default configuration is different from the upstream default configuration, and split into several files optimized for interaction with Ubuntu tools. The configuration system is fully documented in /usr/share/doc/apache2/README.Debian.gz. Refer to this for the full documentation. Documentation for the web server itself can be found by accessing the manual if the apache2-doc package was installed on this server.

The configuration layout for an Apache2 web server installation on Ubuntu systems is as follows: 

/etc/apache2/
|-- apache2.conf
|       `--  ports.conf
|-- mods-enabled
|       |-- *.load
|       `-- *.conf
|-- conf-enabled
|       `-- *.conf
|-- sites-enabled
|       `-- *.conf
  • apache2.conf is the main configuration file. It puts the pieces together by including all remaining configuration files when starting up the web server.
  • ports.conf is always included from the main configuration file. It is used to determine the listening ports for incoming connections, and this file can be customized anytime.
  • Configuration files in the mods-enabled/, conf-enabled/ and sites-enabled/ directories contain particular configuration snippets which manage modules, global configuration fragments, or virtual host configurations, respectively.
  • They are activated by symlinking available configuration files from their respective *-available/ counterparts. These should be managed by using our helpers a2enmod, a2dismod, a2ensite, a2dissite, and a2enconf, a2disconf . See their respective man pages for detailed information.
  • The binary is called apache2 and is managed using systemd, so to start/stop the service use systemctl start apache2 and systemctl stop apache2, and use systemctl status apache2 and journalctl -u apache2 to check status. system and apache2ctl can also be used for service management if desired. Calling /usr/bin/apache2 directly will not work with the default configuration.
Document Roots

By default, Ubuntu does not allow access through the web browser to any file outside of those located in /var/www, public_html directories (when enabled) and /usr/share (for web applications). If your site is using a web document root located elsewhere (such as in /srv) you may need to whitelist your document root directory in /etc/apache2/apache2.conf.

The default Ubuntu document root is /var/www/html. You can make your own virtual hosts under /var/www.

Reporting Problems

Please use the ubuntu-bug tool to report bugs in the Apache2 package with Ubuntu. However, check existing bug reports before reporting a new bug.

Please report bugs specific to modules (such as PHP and others) to their respective packages, not to the web server itself.

If you are a normal user of this web site and don't know what this page is about, this probably means that the site is currently unavailable due to maintenance. If the problem persists, please contact the site's administrator.

Configuration Overview

Ubuntu's Apache2 default configuration is different from the upstream default configuration, and split into several files optimized for interaction with Ubuntu tools. The configuration system is fully documented in /usr/share/doc/apache2/README.Debian.gz. Refer to this for the full documentation. Documentation for the web server itself can be found by accessing the manual if the apache2-doc package was installed on this server.

The configuration layout for an Apache2 web server installation on Ubuntu systems is as follows: 

/etc/apache2/
|-- apache2.conf
|       `--  ports.conf
|-- mods-enabled
|       |-- *.load
|       `-- *.conf
|-- conf-enabled
|       `-- *.conf
|-- sites-enabled
|       `-- *.conf
  • apache2.conf is the main configuration file. It puts the pieces together by including all remaining configuration files when starting up the web server.
  • ports.conf is always included from the main configuration file. It is used to determine the listening ports for incoming connections, and this file can be customized anytime.
  • Configuration files in the mods-enabled/, conf-enabled/ and sites-enabled/ directories contain particular configuration snippets which manage modules, global configuration fragments, or virtual host configurations, respectively.
  • They are activated by symlinking available configuration files from their respective *-available/ counterparts. These should be managed by using our helpers a2enmod, a2dismod, a2ensite, a2dissite, and a2enconf, a2disconf . See their respective man pages for detailed information.
  • The binary is called apache2 and is managed using systemd, so to start/stop the service use systemctl start apache2 and systemctl stop apache2, and use systemctl status apache2 and journalctl -u apache2 to check status. system and apache2ctl can also be used for service management if desired. Calling /usr/bin/apache2 directly will not work with the default configuration.
Document Roots

By default, Ubuntu does not allow access through the web browser to any file outside of those located in /var/www, public_html directories (when enabled) and /usr/share (for web applications). If your site is using a web document root located elsewhere (such as in /srv) you may need to whitelist your document root directory in /etc/apache2/apache2.conf.

The default Ubuntu document root is /var/www/html. You can make your own virtual hosts under /var/www.

Reporting Problems

Please use the ubuntu-bug tool to report bugs in the Apache2 package with Ubuntu. However, check existing bug reports before reporting a new bug.

Please report bugs specific to modules (such as PHP and others) to their respective packages, not to the web server itself.

## userdir
<IfModule mod_userdir.c>
	UserDir public_html
	UserDir disabled root
	<Directory /home/*/public_html>
		AllowOverride FileInfo AuthConfig Limit Indexes
		Options MultiViews Indexes SymLinksIfOwnerMatch IncludesNoExec
		Require method GET POST OPTIONS
	</Directory>
</IfModule>
## wsgi
<IfModule mod_wsgi.c>
</IfModule>
## status
<IfModule mod_status.c>
	<Location /server-status>
		SetHandler server-status
		Require local
	</Location>
	ExtendedStatus On
	<IfModule mod_proxy.c>
		ProxyStatus On
	</IfModule>
</IfModule>
## mpm_event
<IfModule mpm_event_module>
	StartServers			 2
	MinSpareThreads		 25
	MaxSpareThreads		 75
	ThreadLimit			 64
	ThreadsPerChild		 25
	MaxRequestWorkers	  150
	MaxConnectionsPerChild   0
</IfModule>
## reqtimeout
<IfModule reqtimeout_module>
	RequestReadTimeout header=20-40,minrate=500
	RequestReadTimeout body=10,minrate=500
</IfModule>
## ssl
<IfModule mod_ssl.c>
	SSLRandomSeed startup builtin
	SSLRandomSeed startup file:/dev/urandom 512
	SSLRandomSeed connect builtin
	SSLRandomSeed connect file:/dev/urandom 512
	AddType application/x-x509-ca-cert .crt
	AddType application/x-pkcs7-crl	.crl
	SSLPassPhraseDialog  exec:/usr/share/apache2/ask-for-passphrase
	SSLSessionCache		shmcb:${APACHE_RUN_DIR}/ssl_scache(512000)
	SSLSessionCacheTimeout  300
	SSLCipherSuite HIGH:!aNULL
	SSLProtocol all -SSLv3
</IfModule>
## setenvif
<IfModule mod_setenvif.c>
	BrowserMatch "Mozilla/2" nokeepalive
	BrowserMatch "MSIE 4\.0b2;" nokeepalive downgrade-1.0 force-response-1.0
	BrowserMatch "RealPlayer 4\.0" force-response-1.0
	BrowserMatch "Java/1\.0" force-response-1.0
	BrowserMatch "JDK/1\.0" force-response-1.0
	BrowserMatch "Microsoft Data Access Internet Publishing Provider" redirect-carefully
	BrowserMatch "MS FrontPage" redirect-carefully
	BrowserMatch "^WebDrive" redirect-carefully
	BrowserMatch "^WebDAVFS/1.[012]" redirect-carefully
	BrowserMatch "^gnome-vfs/1.0" redirect-carefully
	BrowserMatch "^gvfs/1" redirect-carefully
	BrowserMatch "^XML Spy" redirect-carefully
	BrowserMatch "^Dreamweaver-WebDAV-SCM1" redirect-carefully
	BrowserMatch " Konqueror/4" redirect-carefully
	BrowserMatch " Konqueror/5" redirect-carefully
	BrowserMatch " dolphin/" redirect-carefully
</IfModule>
## negotiation
<IfModule mod_negotiation.c>
	LanguagePriority en ca cs da de el eo es et fr he hr it ja ko ltz nl nn no pl pt pt-BR ru sv tr zh-CN zh-TW
	ForceLanguagePriority Prefer Fallback
</IfModule>
## proxy
<IfModule mod_proxy.c>
</IfModule>

`/app/submission/replica.nix` is written. It builds and boots, and the web, PHP, database and `sudo` behaviour checked out below. The tenants' CGI scripts don't run as the tenants, so it isn't a full drop-in. I also ran out of time to finish a few checks.

I rebuilt and rebooted the VM after each fix. The last edit, `services.logrotate.checkConfig = false`, passed `check-replica` but I did not rebuild or boot after it. That edit exists only to silence a `logrotate-checkconf` unit that was still failing at the last boot, so the final build is unconfirmed.

**What I reproduced from the reference:**
- **Accounts:** `amber` (uid 1101) and `cobalt` (uid 1102) are members of group `tenants`, with locked passwords. Their home directories, `private/token`, `public_html/index.html` and `cgi-bin/hello.py` are recreated on first boot. `/srv/node` holds the "node service" page.
- **Apache:**
  - The `amber`, `cobalt` and `node` virtual hosts, including the `.alt.test` aliases.
  - Port 80 redirects to HTTPS and the ACME challenge path redirects to `acme.node.test`.
  - Userdir, CGI, WSGI and per-tenant `.php` handling, with `node.test/~user` redirecting to the user's own host.
  - The reference's module list and per-tenant logs under `/var/log/web`.
- **PHP-FPM:** one pool per tenant, with the reference's sockets, limits, `open_basedir` and `NODE_LABEL`.
- **Databases:** MariaDB and PostgreSQL both have empty `amber` and `cobalt` databases, with the same password hashes and the same login settings. PostgreSQL also has the same connect restrictions.
- **memcached:** it listens on 127.0.0.1:11211 with 32 MB and UDP off, as the user `memcache`.
- **System settings:**
  - The `sudo` rules let each tenant read their own web logs. I left out the `cobalt-deploy.disabled` rule because it is inactive on the reference.
  - The `@tenants` resource limits, the `web` logrotate rule and the three extra `/etc/hosts` names.
  - SSH has password login off and X11 forwarding on.
  - The firewall is off, the hostname is `node17` and the time zone is UTC.

**Checked on the candidate VM:**
- Amber's `hello.py` served over HTTPS.
- Cobalt's index page served.
- The `~amber` and HTTP-to-HTTPS redirects.
- A PHP page ran as amber with the right memory limit and `NODE_LABEL`.
- Both MariaDB databases were present.
- Amber could read their own web log through `sudo -g adm cat`.

**Known gaps:**
- **CGI user:** `mod_suexec` isn't available in nixpkgs' Apache. The reference runs tenant CGI scripts as the tenant. Mine run as `www-data`, which could break CGI scripts that write to a tenant's home directory.
- **WSGI:** I tested it only on the reference, where my own test app failed, so the replica's WSGI handler is untested. `mod_wsgi` is configured the same way.
- **Cinc:** I did not reproduce `/opt/cinc`. It is a vendored Chef/Cinc tarball, and I judged it too heavy to rebuild in the time.
- **MariaDB `test` database:** I added a `DROP DATABASE test` to remove it. That was in the second-to-last build and I did not re-check it afterwards.
- **Smaller approximations:**
  - The `AddLanguage` list is shortened.
  - The Apache `ServerAdmin` is set to `root@localhost`, so error pages differ slightly.
  - The memcached log file is skipped.

I stopped the reference VM; the candidate VM was shut down too.
